mainTopic: Moving a מנורה and a נר on שבת: רבי יוחנן's rulings on מוקצה, rabbis' practice with lamps, and the נפטא lamp
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא showing that assembling an object on שבת is not בונה. That knocks down one explanation of why רבי יוחנן forbids moving a מנורה. אביי explains that the case is a מנורה of חוליות. The גמרא then clarifies that this means grooves that only look like sections, and sorts out where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue. Next the גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן can rule like רבי יהודה on מוקצה when an unattributed משנה about a wagon's מוכני seems to follow רבי שמעון. רבי זירא reads that משנה narrowly. A report about רבי's ruling in Deyosfera remains תיקו. Stories show rabbis who held like רבי שמעון but refrained from moving a lamp in the town of a rabbi who forbade it, out of respect. Finally, רב יהודה forbids moving a נפטא lamp while רבה and רב יוסף permit it, and רב אויא defends their reason to רבא: a lamp has תורת כלי and pebbles do not. He begins quoting a supporting ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of a ברייתא that permits assembling and taking apart on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a ברייתא state that a certain object may be assembled and taken apart on שבת. This undercuts the idea that moving a מנורה is forbidden because of בונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is permitted to set it up, and permitted to take it apart, on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא. That ברייתא allows an object to be put together and taken apart on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא suggested that the problem with moving a מנורה is that its parts might come apart and someone would put them back together, which is בונה. This ברייתא shows that putting such an object together on שבת is not considered building. If so, a מנורה should certainly not be a building problem, so that explanation collapses.

keyTerms.meaning: to set it up / assemble it

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the END of a quotation that began on the previous amud. It is not a new teaching. It is the evidence that knocks down the 'building' explanation.

phrases.english: it is permitted to set it up
and it is permitted to take it apart on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge begun on the previous amud
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יוחנן forbids moving a מנורה because of בונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If assembling an object on שבת is allowed and is not building, the same must be true of a מנורה.

steps.title: אביי: the case is a מנורה made of separate sections
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רבי יוחנן's prohibition refers to a מנורה built from חוליות, detachable sections.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: it is talking about a מנורה made of sections.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a new reason for רבי יוחנן's prohibition. The case is a מנורה made of separate pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מנורה made of real sections can fall apart when it is moved, and a person might then reassemble it. Making a usable כלי out of loose pieces is more serious than ordinary assembly. Because of that worry, moving it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
It refers to one made of sections.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 1 knocked down
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The prohibition applies to any מנורה because of בונה
steps.terutzMaskana: The prohibition applies to a מנורה made of detachable sections

steps.title: Then why would ריש לקיש permit it?
steps.stepSummary: If the case is a sectioned מנורה, it is hard to see why ריש לקיש would permit moving it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the reason of רבי שמעון בן לקיש, who permits it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's explanation. If there is a real danger of the pieces separating, why would ריש לקיש allow moving it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's case seems to carry an obvious risk. That makes it difficult to explain the lenient side of the מחלוקת, since no one should permit a מנורה that is likely to come apart.

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ דְּשָׁרֵי?
phrases.english: what is the reason of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, who permits it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's explanation that the case is a מנורה of real sections
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real sectioned מנורה should be forbidden by everyone, so ריש לקיש's leniency makes no sense.

steps.title: 'Sections' means grooves that look like sections
steps.stepSummary: The word חוליות here means a מנורה that only looks sectioned because it has grooves.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'sections'? Something like sections, meaning it has grooves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי. The מנורה is not really made of pieces. It only has grooves that make it look that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the argument is no longer about a real danger. It is about whether we make a rabbinic גזירה because the grooved מנורה resembles a real sectioned one. Now ריש לקיש's leniency is reasonable.

phrases.english: What is meant by 'sections'?
Something resembling sections,
meaning it has grooves in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by reinterpreting אביי's word
steps.terutzMaskana: חוליות means grooves that only look like sections

steps.title: Summary: which מנורות are forbidden and where the argument lies
steps.stepSummary: Everyone forbids a real sectioned מנורה of any size, and everyone forbids a large grooved one by גזירה. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue only about a small grooved מנורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore: a real sectioned מנורה, large or small, may not be moved. A large one with grooves is also forbidden, as a decree because of a large sectioned one. They argue about a small one with grooves: one Sage holds we decree, and the other holds we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the full picture. It sorts the cases and shows that the מחלוקת is limited to one narrow case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Large מנורות are often made of real sections, so a large grooved one could be mistaken for one, and everyone forbids it. Small מנורות are usually not made of sections. רבי יוחנן still decrees on the small grooved one, while ריש לקיש says people will realize its grooves are only decoration.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic decree because of (a similar case)

steps.whatToRemember: Real sections: forbidden for everyone. Large with grooves: forbidden for everyone by גזירה. Small with grooves: רבי יוחנן forbids (גזירה) and ריש לקיש permits.

phrases.english: Therefore: one of real sections,
whether large or small,
it is forbidden to move it.
A large one that has grooves is also forbidden,
as a decree because of a large one of real sections.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בִּקְטַנָּה דְּאִית בָּהּ חִידְקֵי:
phrases.english: Where they argue is about a small one that has grooves:
one Sage (רבי יוחנן) holds that we decree,
and the other Sage (ריש לקיש) holds that we do not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical summary out of step 4
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש is limited to a small grooved מנורה, and it turns on whether we make a גזירה.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really rule that way, given his rule about unattributed משניות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוחנן could rule like רבי יהודה, since he holds that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי יוחנן said: the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new challenge against רבי יוחנן's ruling in favor of רבי יהודה, who holds of מוקצה. This step sets up the challenge, and the next step brings the משנה it relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן has a general rule: when a משנה is stated without a name, the הלכה follows it. If an unattributed משנה can be shown to follow רבי שמעון's lenient view, then רבי יוחנן contradicts his own rule.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The halacha follows an unattributed mishna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to רבי יוחנן's position
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי יהודה (who holds of מוקצה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own rule of הלכה כסתם משנה should push him toward an unattributed משנה that follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: The משנה about a wagon's detachable base
steps.stepSummary: An unattributed משנה rules that a wagon's detachable base (מוכני) is separate from the wagon for טומאה purposes, and that the wagon may not be pulled on שבת while money is on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: its base, when it is detachable, is not connected to it, is not measured with it, does not protect with it in a tent containing a corpse, and one may not drag it on שבת while there is money on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the unattributed משנה that the challenge is built on. The key line is the last one, about not pulling the wagon on שבת while money is on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three rulings concern טומאה: the detachable base counts as a separate unit. The final ruling ties the שבת prohibition to money being on the wagon right now. The next step draws an inference from that wording.

keyTerms.meaning: the wheeled base/undercarriage of a wagon
a tent/covering over a corpse (טומאה law)

phrases.english: And we learned in a mishna:
its undercarriage, when it is detachable,
is not considered connected to it,
and is not measured together with it,
and does not protect together with it in a tent over a corpse,
and one may not drag it on Shabbat
when there is money on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the סתם משנה needed for step 6's challenge
steps.raayaObject: That a סתם משנה follows רבי שמעון regarding מוקצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the wagon's מוכני

steps.title: Inference: once the money is gone, the wagon may be moved
steps.stepSummary: The משנה implies that without money on it the wagon may be moved, even if money was on it at בין השמשות. That is רבי שמעון's view, not רבי יהודה's.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if there is no money on it, it is permitted, even though money was on it during twilight?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the inference that completes the challenge. The משנה seems to allow moving the wagon once the money is removed, even if it was there at the start of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that an object that was מוקצה at בין השמשות stays forbidden all שבת. The משנה permits the wagon anyway, which matches רבי שמעון. So רבי יוחנן's rule of following a סתם משנה should make him rule like רבי שמעון, not like רבי יהודה.
steps.confusionAlert: The משנה never says this outright. The challenge comes from inferring the opposite case from the words 'when there is money on it'.

phrases.english: This implies: if there is no money on it, it is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲווֹ עָלֶיהָ בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת?
phrases.english: even though there was money on it at twilight?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge using the משנה from step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי יהודה on מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סתם משנה implies there is no lasting מוקצה from בין השמשות, which is רבי שמעון's view, so רבי יוחנן should follow it.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the משנה means no money was there all of twilight
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא reads the משנה as dealing only with a wagon that had no money on it during בין השמשות, so it does not have to follow רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Let our משנה be speaking of a case where there was no money on it for all of twilight, so as not to break the words of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge by narrowing the case of the משנה. The wagon never became מוקצה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no money was on the wagon at בין השמשות, it was never set aside, so even רבי יהודה permits moving it. The משנה then proves nothing for רבי שמעון. רבי זירא openly admits he chose this reading to protect רבי יוחנן's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: so as not to break (contradict) his words

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's ruling like רבי יהודה is preserved by reading the wagon משנה as a case where no money was there at בין השמשות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא will sometimes read a משנה narrowly so that an אמורא's established rulings stay consistent.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: תְּהֵא מִשְׁנָתֵינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ עָלֶיהָ מָעוֹת
phrases.english: Let our mishna refer to where there was no money on it
throughout all of twilight,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁבּוֹר דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.
phrases.english: so as not to break the words of Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 6–8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה permits the wagon even if money was on it at בין השמשות (like רבי שמעון)
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה deals only with a wagon that had no money on it during בין השמשות, which fits רבי יהודה too

steps.title: רבי's ruling in Deyosfera
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reports that רבי went to Deyosfera and ruled about a מנורה like רבי שמעון's view about a נר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: One time רבי went to Deyosfera, and he ruled about a candelabrum like רבי שמעון ruled about a lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a short report about a practical ruling that רבי gave about moving a מנורה on שבת. The wording is unclear, and the next step will ask what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a lamp that has gone out may be moved on שבת, because he does not accept this kind of מוקצה. The report connects רבי's ruling on a מנורה to that view, but it does not say exactly how.

keyTerms.meaning: Deyosfera, a town that רבי visited
He gave a practical halachic ruling
A candelabrum, often large and made of sections

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One time Rebbi went to Deyosfera,
phrases.notes: רבי here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: and he ruled regarding a candelabrum like Rabbi Shimon regarding a lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: פַּעַם אַחַת הָלַךְ רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a practical ruling of רבי about a מנורה, connecting back to the מנורה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ruled about a מנורה in some connection to רבי שמעון's lenient view about a נר.

steps.title: What exactly did רבי rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי permitted the מנורה like רבי שמעון's נר, or forbade the מנורה and separately permitted the נר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Did he rule about the מנורה like רבי שמעון about a נר, meaning he permitted it? Or perhaps he ruled about the מנורה to forbid it, and he ruled like רבי שמעון about a נר to permit it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how to read רבי's ruling, because the words can be understood in two ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading 1: רבי treated the מנורה like רבי שמעון's lamp, so moving it is permitted. Reading 2: these were two separate rulings. The מנורה is forbidden, probably because of its sections, and the simple נר is permitted like רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them: a question raised in the בית מדרש

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹרָה בִּמְנוֹרָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּנֵר — לְהֶיתֵּרָא,
phrases.english: Did he rule regarding a candelabrum like Rabbi Shimon regarding a lamp, to permit,
or perhaps he ruled regarding the candelabrum to forbid,
and like Rabbi Shimon regarding a lamp, to permit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the report in step 10 actually means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was רבי's ruling about the מנורה lenient, or was it strict, with a separate lenient ruling about the נר?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The question is left as תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot decide between the two readings, so it leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles what רבי meant. The report of his ruling therefore cannot be used to prove either side.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 11 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It remains unknown whether רבי permitted moving a מנורה.

steps.title: Guests moved a lamp and their hosts were upset
steps.stepSummary: רב מלכיא moved a lamp at רבי שמלאי's house, and רבי יוסי גלילאה moved one in רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's town. Both hosts were upset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מלכיא came to רבי שמלאי's house and moved a lamp, and רבי שמלאי was upset. רבי יוסי גלילאה came to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's town and moved a lamp, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא was upset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells two stories in which a visiting rabbi moved a lamp on שבת and the local rabbi was annoyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guests held like רבי שמעון, that a lamp may be moved. The hosts held like רבי יהודה, that it is מוקצה. The hosts were upset because the guests acted against the local rabbi's ruling in his own place.

keyTerms.meaning: To his place, meaning the town where he was the authority

phrases.aramaic: רַב מַלְכִּיָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי
phrases.english: Rav Malkiya happened to come to Rabbi Simlai's house
and moved a lamp,
and Rabbi Simlai was upset.
Rabbi Yosei the Galilean happened to come
to the place of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina,
he moved a lamp
and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina was upset.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מַלְכִּיָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַבִּי שִׂמְלַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי's ruling to stories about how rabbis acted with lamps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Local rabbis who forbade moving a lamp objected when visitors moved one in their place.

steps.title: רבי אבהו acted differently in different towns
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו moved a lamp in רבי יהושע בן לוי's town but not in רבי יוחנן's town.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אבהו came to רבי יהושע בן לוי's place, he would move a lamp. When he came to רבי יוחנן's place, he would not move a lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that רבי אבהו changed his behavior depending on whose town he was in. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי permitted moving a lamp, like רבי שמעון. רבי יוחנן forbade it, like רבי יהודה. רבי אבהו's inconsistency looks puzzling.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu, when he happened to come
to the place of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
would move a lamp.
When he happened to come to the place of Rabbi Yochanan,
he would not move a lamp.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ כִּי אִיקְּלַע לְאַתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another story, this time with a visitor who changed his own behavior.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו moved a lamp in one rabbi's town and refrained in another's.

steps.title: Which view did רבי אבהו hold?
steps.stepSummary: Either way, רבי אבהו should be consistent: always like רבי יהודה or always like רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if he holds like רבי יהודה, let him act like רבי יהודה everywhere. If he holds like רבי שמעון, let him act like רבי שמעון everywhere!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו's behavior as inconsistent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's halachic view should not change from town to town. If he truly holds the lamp is מוקצה, he should never move it. If he holds it is not, he could move it anywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you want: an either-way challenge

phrases.english: Whichever way you want it?
If he holds like Rabbi Yehuda,
let him act like Rabbi Yehuda.
If he holds like Rabbi Shimon,
let him act like Rabbi Shimon!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inconsistency reported in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's different behavior in different towns
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A halachic view should produce the same practice everywhere, so behavior that changes by location seems to make no sense.

steps.title: He held like רבי שמעון but honored רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו held like רבי שמעון, but out of respect for רבי יוחנן he did not move a lamp in his town.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he holds like רבי שמעון, and only out of respect for רבי יוחנן did he not do so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אבהו's real view was lenient, but he held back in רבי יוחנן's town out of respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One does not act against the ruling of the local authority in his own place, even if one disagrees. So refraining was a matter of respect, not a change of opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth: introduces the true position
Because of his honor, out of respect

phrases.english: Really, he holds like Rabbi Shimon,
and because of the honor of Rabbi Yochanan
is why he would not do it.

steps.whatToRemember: A visitor should not act leniently against the local rabbi's ruling in his place, even when the visitor's own view is lenient.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the either-way challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates halachic opinion from practical conduct done out of respect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His changing behavior showed he was unsure or inconsistent about the law.
steps.terutzMaskana: He held like רבי שמעון. Refraining in רבי יוחנן's town was only out of respect.

steps.title: רב יהודה: an oil lamp may be moved, a נפטא lamp may not
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה permits moving an oil lamp but forbids moving a נפטא lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: An oil lamp may be moved. A נפטא lamp may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling that splits lamps into two types.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oil lamp may be moved, like רבי שמעון. A נפטא lamp smells bad, so it is used only for lighting. Since its only use is forbidden on שבת, it is treated as מוקצה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
An oil lamp is permitted to move,
a naphtha lamp is forbidden to move.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about which kinds of lamps may be moved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An oil lamp may be moved on שבת. A נפטא lamp may not.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף permit a נפטא lamp too
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף hold that a נפטא lamp may also be moved, since it can be used to cover a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both said: A נפטא lamp may also be moved, since it is fit to cover a vessel with it.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים disagree with רב יהודה and permit moving a נפטא lamp as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a smelly lamp has a permitted use: it can be put over a dish as a cover. Because of that permitted use, it is not completely set aside, so it may be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is fit (for some use)

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both said:
a naphtha lamp, too, is permitted to move,
since it is fit to cover a vessel with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יהודה's ruling on a נפטא lamp.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נפטא lamp may be moved because it has a permitted use: covering a vessel.

steps.title: רב אויא dirties רבא's bed
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא came to רבא with muddy shoes and sat on the bed. רבא was upset and wanted to test him with hard questions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא came to רבא's house. His shoes were dirty with mud. He sat on the bed in front of רבא. רבא was upset and wanted to trouble him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a test of the reason given by רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא was annoyed that his bed was dirtied, so he decided to challenge רב אויא with difficult questions. The questions come in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rav Avya happened to come to Rava's house.
His feet (shoes) were dirty with mud.
He sat on the bed before Rava.
Rava was upset, and wanted to trouble him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Story setup leading into an analysis of רבה and רב יוסף's reason.

steps.title: רבא asks the reason for permitting a נפטא lamp
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב אויא why רבה and רב יוסף permit moving a נפטא lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is the reason that רבה and רב יוסף both said a נפטא lamp may also be moved?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens his test by asking רב אויא to explain the lenient ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא asks for the reasoning so that he can then attack it.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is the reason
that Rabba and Rav Yosef both said
a naphtha lamp, too, is permitted to move?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא begins the test promised in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a נפטא lamp may be moved.

steps.title: Because it can cover a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא answers that the lamp is fit to cover a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since it is fit to cover a vessel with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא gives the reason already stated by רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permitted use of covering a vessel keeps the lamp from being מוקצה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Since it is fit to cover a vessel with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הוֹאִיל וְחַזְיָא לְכַסּוֹיֵי בַּהּ מָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It can be used as a cover for a vessel, which is a permitted use.

steps.title: Then pebbles should be movable too
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects: if that reason works, all pebbles in a yard could be moved, since they too can cover a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, all pebbles in the yard may be moved, since they are fit to cover a vessel with them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the reason by showing it would permit something everyone forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pebbles are clearly מוקצה on שבת. Yet a pebble could also cover a vessel. So 'fit to cover a vessel' seems too weak a reason to permit moving something.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: introduces an unacceptable result

phrases.english: But if so,
all pebbles in the yard may be moved,
since they are fit to cover a vessel with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, כׇּל צְרוֹרוֹת שֶׁבֶּחָצֵר מִטַּלְטְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'fit to cover a vessel'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: the same reason would permit moving pebbles, which are clearly forbidden.

steps.title: A lamp is a כלי, pebbles are not
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא answers that a lamp has the status of a כלי, while pebbles do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This one (the lamp) has the status of a vessel. These (the pebbles) do not have the status of a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא draws a distinction that answers רבא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamp is a manufactured utensil, a כלי, so even a small permitted use is enough to allow moving it. Pebbles are raw material, not a כלי. They are not permitted just because they could be used, unless they were designated for a use before שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The halachic status of a utensil

steps.confusionAlert: The 'covering a vessel' reason works only because the lamp is already a כלי. It does not mean that anything usable may be moved.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This one has the status of a vessel upon it.
These do not have the status of a vessel upon them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the pebbles challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases (a כלי versus raw material)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any object with a possible permitted use may be moved, including pebbles.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an object with the status of a כלי, like a lamp, becomes movable through a permitted use. Pebbles do not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule of מוקצה: having the status of a כלי is a key factor in whether an object may be moved.

steps.title: רב אויא begins bringing a ברייתא as proof
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא introduces a ברייתא to support his distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was it not taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. רב אויא is about to quote a ברייתא, which appears on the next amud, to back up his distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase signals that a known teaching supports the idea that a כלי has special leniencies for moving on שבת. The actual source comes right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: Was it not taught (in a ברייתא)? Introduces a supporting source

phrases.english: Was it not taught:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces support for the distinction made in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction that a כלי has leniencies that raw materials like pebbles do not
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא, quoted on the next amud
